title: Co-sell package and billing SKU runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
This runbook is a working draft to align product, finance, partnerships, and engineering on the co-sell package we’ll publish across cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). Focus areas: SKU design, metering dimensions, trial activation flow, listing copy prerequisites, and publisher portal preflight checks.

Audience
- GTM (partner managers, marketplace ops)
- Product (pricing, packaging owners)
- Finance (billing mapping, revenue recognition)
- Infra/Platform (metering, telemetry)
- Legal (contracting clauses for marketplace offers)

High-level constraints and assumptions
- We publish the same logical product tiers across marketplaces but map to provider-specific SKUs and metering dimensions.
- Core billing model for public listing: subscription (monthly) + optional metered addons (tokens or inference-minutes).
- We must support 14-day trial activation via publisher portal (or equivalent) for Azure/AWS; GCP will require promo code flow.
- All listing assets must be finalized two weeks before publisher portal submission to allow legal/compliance review.

Offer / SKU strategy (proposal)
- Free Sandbox (SKU: RW-SBX-001)
  - Purpose: developer get-started, limited tokens and no SLA.
  - Billing: free, metered cap hard limit (10k tokens / month).
- Starter (SKU: RW-START-100)
  - Purpose: early-stage apps, dev+small prod tests.
  - Pricing: $99 / month base, 100k included tokens, overage $0.0008/token.
  - Metering dimension: tokens.
- Scale (SKU: RW-SCALE-1K)
  - Purpose: production, higher throughput.
  - Pricing: $999 / month base, 1M included tokens, custom overage tiers.
  - Optional: dedicated inference reserved pool addon (metered as GPU-hours).
- Enterprise (SKU: RW-ENT-TAILORED)
  - Purpose: committed reserved capacity (Dedicated), private deployment add-ons.
  - Pricing: negotiated via sales (list mapping required for publisher portal).

Metering dimensions (mapping notes)
- Token-based metering (primary): per-token consumed by generation API.
- GPU-hours (optional addon): for reserved capacity / Dedicated features.
- Seats/API-keys (legacy): not primary but supported for partner listings that require seat counts.

Mapping to provider metering examples (implementation TODOs)
- AWS Marketplace: use product codes for each SKU; subscribe via monthly SaaS contract. Need to coordinate with platform-engineering to emit MeteringRecord for token consumption.
- Azure Marketplace: Plan definitions map to SKUs; trials handled via Publisher Trial offer. Confirm trial provisioning callback URL and entitlement sync.
- GCP Marketplace: Use license-keys + usage reporting; promo code flow required for trials.

Trial activation flow (developer experience)
- Goal: < 90s activation for Sandbox/Starter trials.
- Steps:
  1) User clicks "Try on [Marketplace]" -> redirected to publisher onboarding flow.
  2) Marketplace returns entitlement callback -> Redwood creates trial org and issues API key.
  3) Welcome email + quickstart guide with sample curl and SDK snippets.
  4) Telemetry event fired: marketplace_trial_activated with partner and plan metadata.

- Edge cases to handle: callback retries, duplicate entitlements, email deliverability failures.

Listing copy and assets (requirements)
- Short tagline (<= 140 chars) that emphasizes predictable inference economics and multi-deployment options.
- 1–2 paragraph description: product summary, who it’s for, highlight features (low-latency, batching, private deployments).
- Screenshots: Console product page (dashboard), per-route latency graph, billing breakdown screenshot (min 1200x675).
- Logo: SVG + 512px PNG, transparent background.
- Video: optional 60–90s explainer (MP4, <50MB).
- Security/compliance bullet list: SOC2, ISO27001 (if applicable), VPC + KMS integrations.

Copy draft (short + long) — working text to iterate with comms
- Short: "Fast, predictable LLM inference for production apps — hosted, dedicated, or privately deployed."
- Long: "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime to serve modern LLMs with predictable latency and cost. Ship generative features with confidence: automatic batching, KV/prefix caching, and built-in fallbacks keep your app online while optimizing per-token economics. Choose hosted for fast time-to-value, Dedicated for committed throughput, or Private for regulated workloads. Integrated observability and rollout controls make production rollouts safe and measurable."

Publisher portal preflight checklist (operational) — items to complete before submission
- [ ] Finalized SKU table (provider mappings + pricing) — finance signoff
- [ ] Billing test harness: integration tests exercising metering events (token usage, GPU-hours)
- [ ] Trial callback endpoint implemented + smoke-tested
- [ ] Listing creatives (logo, screenshots, video) uploaded to shared asset bucket
- [ ] Legal checklist: marketplace CLA reviewed, refund policy drafted
- [ ] Security blurb validated with security-and-compliance team
- [ ] App/Service owner assigned for publisher support queue (on-call rotations)

Revenue recognition & billing notes (finance)
- For SaaS-subscription offers, revenue recognized monthly after entitlement activation. Trials -> convert events must be tracked for ARR conversion metrics.
- Metered overages: ensure metering records reconcile with invoices (platform-engineering to provide daily reconciliation job).
- For Dedicated/Private (contracted): link to contract id and provisioning ticket (Solutions Eng).

Telemetry and observability (engineering)
- Required events: marketplace_checkout_initiated, marketplace_trial_activated, marketplace_subscription_converted, marketplace_overage_billed
- Logs to include provider_plan_id, marketplace_id (aws|azure|gcp), customer_org_id, sku_id, tokens_consumed, gpu_hours_consumed, invoice_id (when available).

Open questions / unresolved
- Q1: Do we want per-token pricing across all marketplaces or provider-specific adjustments? (Finance preference: consistent list price; discounts/commissions negotiated separately.)
- Q2: How to handle multi-region billing customers (GCP versus AWS residency)? Needs legal + tax review.
- Q3: Trial length parity across providers (14 days vs 30 days)? Recommendation: standardize on 14d to simplify entitlements.

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Miguel: draft final SKU pricing table and run initial elasticity checks (due 2026-02-20)
- Darya: validate trial callback endpoints with infra and produce smoke test runbook (due 2026-02-17)
- Samir: prepare publisher portal staging submission and collect screenshots (due 2026-02-24)
- Aisha (owner): consolidate legal feedback and schedule sign-off sync (2026-02-15)

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider a "pay-as-you-go" token-only listing for non-committal customers in a second wave.
- Keep a single canonical SKU->provider mapping document in github for traceability.
- If marketplace commissions materially change LTV, we may prefer redirecting customers to hosted API for certain segments.

Appendix: useful links and references
- Marketplace onboarding Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTM/Marketplace+Onboarding+Checklist
- Billing integration ticket: JIRA-PLAT-4532
- Marketplace assets repo: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets

End of draft — this is intentionally a working document. Add comments inline, flag items as blockers, and update the SKU table in the linked GitHub PR when pricing is finalized.
